newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Vols firm on dollar's persistent strength.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Vols firm on dollar's persistent strength.

text.p: Implied volatilities in dollar/pair options stuck mostly firmer Wednesday, with continued dollar/yen strength also wiping out much of the recent strong skew toward yen calls.
"Vols are still pretty firm. One-month yen is right around 10.7/11.0," said a bank options trader.
That compares to about 10.6/10.9 percent late Tuesday and follows a brief pullback to 9.7/10.0 earlier Wednesday.
Brokers and analysts said the dollar's persistent push to higher levels had caught many players off-guard, resulting in some rethinking of positions and market expectations.
"I think people all of a sudden got hammered because they thought the yen was going to continue to strengthen or at least hold that 113.50-115.00 range," said an options analyst.

"I think you had lot of people who were long yen, thinking we were going to have a little bit of a rally with Sakakibara's new position of power, and I think they just got hurt a little bit," he added. "It (dollar rise) just crept right by them, and all of a sudden you wake up and you're at 116 not 114."
Eisuke Sakakibara, formerly director of the Japanese Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, was promoted this week to vice finance minister for international affairs.

The options trader said the dollar/yen risk reversal has come in "big-time" in the last few days, toward 0.1/0.4 point still favoring yen calls from about 0.6 traded late Tuesday and off from a peak near 3.0 points last week.

"Basically the cross-currents are (that) there's a lot of investor interest to buy dollar calls/yen puts, partially offsetting those Japanese interests to sell dollars, sell options," he said. "But certainly the supply/demand relationship is definitely in favor of the dollar calls right now. That's pushing the risk-reversal in (from) strongly in favor of (yen) calls, much closer to par."

In one-month marks, vols held near 10.5/10.8 percent, slightly below the 10.7/10.9 seen late Tuesday and little changed from Wednesday's early European levels. The risk reversal still favored mark puts, at 0.35/0.65 point.

Brokers said action Wednesday concentrated in spot again after Tuesday's busy options turnover, although sterling continued drawing interest. One-month cable returned toward Tuesday's 10.0/10.4 percent level after a dip early Wednesday.
"There's still a lot of sterling put buying interest around, six months and longer," added the trader. "I think once again it's investor-based (interest.)"
